SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a high-quality franchise with a genuine competitive moat — vertically integrated distribution across 5,000+ stores, dominant ~69% U.S. Paint Stores market share, and proven pricing power (7% price increase effective Jan 2026). FY2025 delivered record adjusted EPS of $11.43, OCF of $3.45B (+9.4% YoY), and Q4 EBITDA margin expanded 120bps to 17.7%. FY2026 guidance of $11.50–$11.90 EPS signals continued growth. However, the stock at ~32.7x P/E trades at a premium to the ~26x chemicals peer average, and the 3.1% earnings yield sits below the 4.34% 10-year Treasury — offering no margin of safety. Leverage is elevated at D/E 2.185x ($9.67B debt vs $4.43B equity). WTI crude at $99.27 (+64% over lookback) is a material raw-material headwind for a coatings manufacturer. Demand remains soft — management noted 'several end markets may not improve until 2026,' and housing starts have been down YoY for three consecutive months. The P/E at 32.7x is near the low end of its 12-month range (29.4x–37.1x), providing modest relative value within its own history, but the absolute level still embeds growth expectations that require volume recovery to justify. Q1 2026 earnings on April 28 is a near-term catalyst — consensus EPS $2.28 on $5.57B revenue — that will reveal whether the 7% price increase is flowing through and volumes are stabilizing. Net: excellent franchise, solid execution, but fairly priced for the growth embedded; the oil headwind and demand softness cap upside. Mildly positive on balance.
key_factors: Dominant franchise: ~69.4% U.S. Paint Stores industry revenue share, 5,000+ company-owned stores, vertically integrated distribution with deep professional-customer relationships
Record FY2025 earnings: adjusted diluted EPS $11.43, net sales $23.57B (+2.1% YoY), OCF $3.45B (+9.4% YoY), Q4 EBITDA margin expanded 120bps to 17.7%
FY2026 guidance: adjusted EPS $11.50–$11.90; analysts expect ~$12 for FY2026 and ~$13 for FY2027
Pricing power demonstrated: 7% professional price increase effective January 1, 2026; gross margin ~48-49% sustained across quarters
Valuation near low end of range: P/E 32.7x vs 12-month range 29.4x–37.1x, but still at premium to ~26x chemicals peer average; earnings yield 3.1% below 10-year Treasury 4.34%
Elevated leverage: D/E 2.185x ($9.67B debt, $4.43B equity); net debt/EBITDA 2.2x at FY2024 year-end
Raw material headwind: WTI crude at $99.27 (+64% over lookback) — direct input-cost risk for petrochemical-dependent coatings
Demand softness: 'several end markets may not improve until 2026'; housing starts down YoY for 3 consecutive months; CBG Q3 2025 sales declined 2.6% YoY
Near-term catalyst: Q1 2026 earnings April 28 — consensus EPS $2.28, revenue $5.565B — will test price-increase flow-through and volume stabilization
48th consecutive annual dividend increase declared April 22, 2026; $2.5B returned to shareholders in FY2024
